E039 places group-1 BN on 15×15 maps and shows it costs nothing, so H6.3 is narrowed to the 31×31 tensors before the pool and lowered to 0.3.\n- **H6.1 and H6.2 (small maps, tile alignment):** downgraded. Map-size arithmetic explains E024 and E021 without them.\n- **H6.4 (new):** the 24-channel whitening output makes group-1 conv1 inefficient. It has a profiler test (H6.4.1) and a math-identical pad-to-32-channels test (H6.4.2).\n\n**Committee counterexamples**\n- E025 and E026 time: both runs were built on E023 while the forecasts assumed E016/E017.\n- E028 time: explained by H6.3 or H6.4.\n- E030 accuracy: the Lookahead reset is part of the gain (H1.3).\n- E032 accuracy: label smoothing 0.3 shapes the averaged solution (H1.3).\n- E031 time: selection removes steps, and time follows steps (H2.7 and H5.2, both new).\n\n**Other new branches**\n- **Stem freeze:** H2.6.7 (freeze at ~71%, right after the switch to 32 px, to locate E037's cliff) and H2.6.8 (a staggered group-2 freeze).\n- **Proxy-free loss selection:** H2.7 and H2.7.1, with E031 as evidence.\n- **Batch size and step count:** H5.2 and H5.2.1 (step count carries early accuracy), set up as the opposite prediction to H5.1.3. H5.1.4 (late batch growth) is from the Seesaw paper. H5 is raised to 0.3, and H5.1.x are rebased to E036 with 20-seed judging.\n\n**Other confidence changes**\n- H1.3.6 (BN recompute) rises to 0.45: the search confirmed in airbench's code that Lookahead lerps the BN buffers, and the committee is split, so it needs a decisive 20-seed test.\n- H1.2.3 and H1.5.4 now point to code reads for the Newton-Schulz step count and filter renormalization.\n- Lowered: H1.4, H1.5.5, H1.5.8, H2.3.4, H2.4.\n\nH5 and H6 stay open as Lvl1 hypotheses."}

updates.statement: The number of epochs needed to reach 75% (sample efficiency) sets most of the wall time. Backbone, optimizer and regularization choices that cut epochs-to-target are the main lever. Together with resizing, compile, averaging and stem backward truncation, they give about 11x over the organizer's 40-epoch ResNet9 baseline (59.30 s on an A100 80GB PCIe, taken from forks of the competition repo and not run in this loop). That is 5.31 s at the E036 tip, which passed the local bar on only 1 of 2 builds (0.7532 in E036, 0.7525 in E038).
updates.reason: The text still described E027 (5.88 s) as the tip. The tip is now E036 at 5.31 s, with the caveat from E038 that it is not reproducibly feasible. The overall claim is unchanged.

updates.statement: At a fixed epoch count, the cost per epoch (systems overhead plus per-layer cost per sample) is a large lever. Levers found so far: compile/fusion (−14%, E004); progressive resizing (−22% E007, −2.9% E026, −3.2% E033); and stem backward truncation, made up of a group-1 freeze over the last 25% of steps (−8.8% with no held-out cost, E028, stacked in E034) and a whitening-bias detach after 20% of steps (−2.4%, E036). Launch overhead is exhausted (E015, E017). Limits: freezing from 60% costs about 0.4–0.56 pp (E037), and folding BN in the frozen phase saves nothing (E039).
updates.reason: E033, E034 and E036 were missing from the lever list, and the E037/E039 limits were not recorded.

E035 removed most of the first-call overhead (−0.035 s on the 3-trial mean). The remaining ~0.07 s in trial 0's prepare depends on the harness process and is ~0.02 s on the mean, so the claim that this cost is comparable to the other levers no longer holds (review). Profiling can reopen it if whitening init turns out to be large.
E035 cut ~0.035 s on the mean, short of the ≥0.05 s prediction. What remains looks tied to the harness and is not worth another run.

E035 tested a different statement: it kept the full whitening set on purpose (bit-identical math) and cut 0.035 s, below 0.05 s. The 5k-subset part was never tested, and it would re-draw trajectories for ~0.01 s, so it is not worth a run.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the accuracy margin: the best time comes from sitting just above the 0.753 3-seed bar while still holding ≥0.75 over 40 seeds. The seeds 0–2 mean is a noisy estimate (offset RMS ~0.20 pp, plus rebuild re-draws of 0.1–0.44 pp per seed). The E036 tip's unbiased population mean is ~0.754: fresh seeds 13–22 give 0.7538, and the pooled 20-seed mean is 0.7547 (SE 0.06). Under the Φ model it therefore passes the local bar about 55–70% of the time, consistent with passing on 1 of 2 builds. Keeps should be gated on a mean of ≥~0.7545 from seeds not used for selection, and the gate should not change between experiments (it has been 0.7535, 0.752 and 0.7545).
updates.reason: Updated to the E036 tip, the fresh-seed estimate from E038, and the review's points on inconsistent gates and rebuild noise.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise has four parts. (a) Rebuild noise: artifacts built without cudagraphs are bit-identical per seed. Max-autotune/cudagraph rebuilds re-draw trajectories partly: per-seed shifts are 0.1–0.44 pp (E036 vs E038; E034 vs E035), while the 3-seed mean moves <0.1 pp across 4 observations, from averaging alone. (b) Seed and test-set noise: per-seed std is 0.15–0.35 pp. (c) Trajectory re-draw: any change to the math or the RNG re-draws every seed, so per-seed differences across recipes carry little information (E025). (d) Winner's curse: seeds 3–12 drove ~10 keeps, and E036's seeds 3–12 mean (0.7557) sits 0.19 pp above fresh seeds 13–22 (0.7538). The SE of a difference between two 10-seed means is ≈0.10–0.14 pp, so most single 10-seed calls of 0.15–0.28 pp are 1–2σ. Changes worth <0.25 pp need 20 seeds per arm, measured against a baseline on unselected seeds.
updates.reason: The review showed that '±0.03 pp rebuild noise' and E019's 'persistent seed×RNG offset' reading are contradicted by E036/E038 and E034/E035. Also added the winner's-curse component measured in E038.

Rebuilds partly re-draw per-seed trajectories (0.1–0.44 pp), so the judge's own build is a fresh draw. The local feasibility of a ~0.754-population tip transfers only probabilistically. The 40-seed 0.75 bar still has ~0.4–0.5 pp headroom.

E038: fresh seeds 13–22 gave 0.7538, 0.19 pp below seeds 3–12, so the 'within 0.15 pp' half fails. The pooled 20-seed mean of 0.7547 is ≥0.753, so the second half holds. This is a mild winner's curse. Re-run on the final candidate.

Dial points unchanged. E041's non-uniform trim reads −0.20 pp against E036's selection seeds but −0.01 pp against fresh seeds 13–22, so the rate ranking is unresolved. Per the review, only rank exchange rates when their CIs separate. E025/E026 time counterexamples: both runs were built on E023 (9.0 true epochs) while the forecasts assumed E016/E017 (9.5), a base mismatch rather than a missing mechanism.

E041 was −0.20 pp against E036's seeds 3–12 (a winner's-curse baseline) but −0.01 pp against the unbiased fresh-seed baseline (0.7538), which would pass the ≤0.1 pp rule. With SE ~0.13 pp neither reading is resolved. Re-test on 20 fresh seeds (H4.4.1).

updates.statement: Progressive resizing is a near-linear time dial for the sizes used (about 0.51/0.71/0.89 s per epoch at 24/28/32 px, E012). The 28 and 32 px phases carry accuracy: dropping the 28 px phase cost −0.68 pp (E018), and shrinking the 32 px tail to 20% cost −0.97 pp (E011, confounded). Early low resolution is cheap: E026 at −0.15 pp and E033 at 0.00 pp for 15–30% of steps at 20 px. The 20 px dose curve is non-monotone (E026 −0.15, E033 0.00, E040 −0.28 against biased baselines), which points to noise rather than a mechanism, so further early-phase claims need 20 seeds. A 26 px middle phase (E024) saved less time than modelled because group 3 stays at 6×6 maps, not because of tile efficiency. Candidate mechanisms for the late-phase loss remain unseparated: (a) low resolution during peak LR; (b) FixRes/BN shift at the final jump; (c) too little 32 px fine-tuning during averaging. The tests H2.3.5, H2.3.7 and H2.6.7 would discriminate.
updates.reason: Reconciled with the review. The E040/E041 'early steps carry accuracy' reading is withdrawn as winner's-curse-confounded. The E024 time explanation is replaced with map-size arithmetic.

E033 tested exactly this statement: 30% of steps at 20 px, −3.2% time, 0.00 pp held-out. That meets both thresholds. E040 tested a different statement (40/0/30/30), now H2.3.8, and does not refute this one.

updates.statement: Truncating the backward pass at the high-resolution stem cuts per-step cost far more than its FLOP share, at little accuracy cost if the stem has trained at 32 px. Evidence: freezing group 1 and the whitening bias for the last 25% of steps saved ~27% per frozen 32 px step with no held-out loss (E028), and it stacked with +0.5 epoch (E034). Detaching the whitening output after 20% of steps saved a further 2.4% with no held-out loss (E036). Limits: a freeze from 60%, before the 28→32 px switch at 70%, cost 0.4–0.56 pp (E037). Putting frozen group-1 BN in eval mode and folding it saved nothing (E039). The source of the saving (conv kernels on small-Cin inputs vs memory-bound traffic) is unprofiled (H6.3, H6.4).
updates.reason: Added E034/E036 support and the E037/E039 limits.
E034: 5.48 s (≤5.75) with a held-out mean of 0.7549 (≥0.7540). Both halves met, and the keep gate was met.
E036: −2.4% time with held-out 0.7557 vs 0.7549 (no loss). The fresh-seed 0.7538 for E036 sits below E034's seeds 3–12 mean, but both baselines carry selection bias. Within noise.

E037: −4.6% time but −0.56 pp held-out, and still ~−0.37 pp against the unbiased fresh baseline (0.7538). Exceeds the 0.15 pp limit well beyond noise. All 4 committee members agree. The cause (no stem training at 32 px vs total lost signal vs steeper anneal) is open; see H2.6.7 and H2.6.6.
E039: −0.6% time, within the 5.31–5.33 s build spread. Group-1 BN sits on 15×15 maps after the pool, so its reductions are not a meaningful cost. All 4 members agree.

updates.statement: The per-MAC cost of the step is not uniform across layers, so a systems or architecture lever worth ≥5% remains at near-identical math. The best-supported locus is the stem. E028 removed group-1 and whitening backward and saved ~27% of a 32 px step, although that backward is only ~13% of step FLOPs. Candidate causes: (a) conv kernels with a small or misaligned channel count, such as the 24-channel whitening output feeding group-1 conv1 (dgrad/wgrad), running at low tensor-core efficiency; (b) memory-bound elementwise and pool traffic on the 31×31 conv1 output. E039 rules out group-1 BN (15×15 maps) as a material cost. The small-map/off-grid regime (H6.1/H6.2) is better explained by map-size arithmetic. No profiler trace has been run in 41 experiments.
updates.reason: The review showed E039 undercuts regime (b) as stated and that E021/E024 point toward big maps being slow, not small ones. Reworded around the stem and the 24-channel conv1 alternative.

E021's sublinear time saving fits E028's finding that group 1 takes more than its MAC share, which leaves less time in group 2 to cut. That points away from 'small maps are slow'. Downgraded until a profile shows per-layer TFLOP/s differences.
The parent mechanism is weakened. Keep as a free by-product of the single profiler trace.
Map-size arithmetic explains E024 without tile effects: group 3 runs at 6×6 at both 26 and 28 px. The off-grid list is incoherent (23/27/31 are odd too, and 320 is a multiple of 64). Downgraded.
The parent is downgraded. Keep only as a by-product of the profiler trace.

updates.statement: On the largest maps (the whitening output and group-1 conv1 output at 31×31, before the first pool), memory-bound kernels (the pool and its backward, elementwise ops) and/or low-efficiency convs take a much larger share of step time than their FLOPs. This explains E028's ~27% per-step saving. Group-1 BN/GELU run after the pool on 15×15 maps and are not the cost (E039).
updates.reason: E039 contradicts the original 'BN/GELU on 31×31 maps' wording. The claim is narrowed to the pre-pool tensors, and the confidence is lowered because the conv-efficiency explanation (H6.4) fits E028 equally well.

updates.statement: In short CIFAR-100 runs, end-of-run averaging is a first-order lever: Lookahead/EMA gave +0.97 pp at E005. The airbench Lookahead schedule is a local optimum on both sides. A harder pull hurt (E025, −0.27 pp held-out), longer free runs hurt (E030, −0.24 pp), and dropping LS late hurt (E032, −0.23 pp), so LS 0.3 regularizes what gets averaged. With averaging on, the final-LR floor does not matter (E009, C0021). The reset probably carries part of the gain (Switch-EMA, C0024). Confirmed in code: airbench's Lookahead lerps and copies back BN running_mean/var along with the weights, so the final BN statistics are a mixture over different fast weights and are never recomputed (search). Untested: BN recomputation (H1.3.6) and plain EMA (H1.3.5).
updates.reason: Folded in E030/E032 and the code confirmation of BN-buffer lerping from the search. E030's counterexample (accuracy below every member's range) is explained by the reset being part of the mechanism. E032's counterexample is explained by LS shaping the averaged solution.

updates.statement: On the E036 tip, recompute BN running statistics for the final averaged weights: one 32 px train-mode forward over ≤5k training images, with BN momentum set so the stats reflect only those batches, inside timed train (<0.1 s). Prediction, judged on 20 seeds not used for selection (13–32) against the E036 baseline on the same seeds: the mean rises by ≥0.15 pp and the per-seed std does not increase. Refuted if the change is ≤0.
updates.reason: The search confirmed the premise in airbench96_faster's code (BN buffers are lerped across fast weights), and PreciseBN (Wu & Johnson) shows EMA stats lag in short, high-LR runs, with 10^3–10^4 samples enough. The committee is split (2 refuted, 2 unknown), so this needs a decisive 20-seed test. Rebased to the E036 tip, and the threshold is lowered to what 20 seeds can resolve.

E032: −0.23 pp held-out vs E027 (whose held-out mean was not selection-inflated, being below its own gate). This is the opposite direction to the prediction, and all 4 members agree. LS 0.3 helps through the end.

E006's +0.66 pp confounds Muon, batch 1024→2000 and an RNG re-draw. The statement's control (SGD tuned at batch 2000) was never run, so E006 is tentative evidence only (E006~ in substance). H1.2.2 is the isolating test.

The search shows both reference recipes (airbench94_muon, Hiverge) use 3 Newton-Schulz steps and that orthogonalization quality is not monotone in accuracy (2606.00371, Polar Express). The port's NS count and renormalization still need a code read, at zero run cost.

The search confirms airbench94_muon renormalizes each filter every step (p.data.mul_(len(p)**0.5/p.norm())), which makes filter wd inert. If the port copies this, the question is settled by reading the code. The read is still unrecorded after being requested in I033.

airbench96 used untuned CIFAR-10 hyperparameters on CIFAR-100 (search), which fits E016. E032 shows LS 0.3 matters late in the run. The E013/E014/E009 'flat' results are re-labelled 'not detected at 3-seed power'.
Hiverge's LS 0.09 comes from a 10-class recipe that uses TTA (search caveat), and E032 shows removing LS late hurts by 0.23 pp. Prior lowered.
The committee expects refutation (2 refuted). Hiverge's jitter values come from a TTA, 10-class recipe.
This sat at 0.70 confidence with no evidence in 41 experiments (review). Lowered to an uninformed prior. Alternating flip is cheap to keep, so testing it is low priority.
The committee expects refutation (2 refuted), and E032 shows weaker LS hurts late. Low priority.
E031 used no proxy, so it does not test this Lvl2. It has been moved to the new proxy-free selection branch. Most of the committee (3) expects refutation because of the proxy's cost.
Committee leans refuted (2 refuted). The extra 0.5× forward is unlikely to pay off on top of the stem freeze.

Tentative indirect evidence that optimizer steps carry accuracy. E033 changed pixels but not steps and was free. E031 (−9% steps, −0.27 pp) and E041 (−5% steps) cost about as much as uniform cuts, though E041 is noise-ambiguous. Batch size has never been varied under Muon since E006. Raised slightly; H5.1.2/H5.1.3 and H5.2.1 are the decisive tests.

updates.statement: On the E036 tip at the same true epoch count, raising batch from 2000 to 2500 (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged, all schedules, including freeze and detach points, kept as step fractions) keeps the 20-seed (13–32) mean within 0.15 pp of E036 on the same seeds and cuts mean time by at least 1.5%.
updates.reason: Rebased to the current tip with a 20-seed unselected baseline. E031/E041 hint that removing steps costs accuracy, which lowers the prior slightly.

updates.statement: On the E036 tip at the same true epoch count, lowering batch from 2000 to 1500 (same scaling rules) raises the 20-seed (13–32) mean by at least 0.2 pp vs E036 on the same seeds, at no more than +4% time. That rate would beat the epoch dial (~1.5 s/pp).
updates.reason: Rebased from E017 to E036 with 20-seed judging, per the review. This is the main untested Lvl1 lever.

updates.statement: On the E036 tip, using batch 3000 in the 20/24 px phases (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged, step counts recomputed) and 2000 at 28/32 px cuts mean time by at least 2% and keeps the 20-seed (13–32) mean within 0.15 pp of E036 on the same seeds. H5.2.1 predicts the opposite, so the two form a decisive pair.
updates.reason: Rebased, and paired with the new competing prediction H5.2.1.

updates.statement: On the E036 tip, dropping the third conv in group 1 (the block that takes more time than its MAC share, per E028) cuts mean time by at least 5% and loses no more than 0.2 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean.
updates.reason: Rebased. Under the freeze, group 1's backward is already skipped for the last 25% of steps, so the expected saving is smaller than the original 8%.

new.statement: Group-1 conv1 takes the 24-channel whitening output (Cin=24, not a multiple of 32/64). Its forward, dgrad and wgrad kernels on 31×31 maps run at low tensor-core efficiency and take a share of step time far above their FLOPs. That share is the main part of what E028/E036 saved by truncating the stem backward, and it is still paid in every unfrozen step.

A torch.profiler trace of one 32 px train step of the E036 tip (full, unfrozen variant) shows group-1 conv1 (forward plus backward) achieving less than half the TFLOP/s of the group-2 convs, and taking at least 10% of step GPU time. One trace also settles H2.2.4, H6.1.1, H6.2.1 and H6.3.1.

Math-identical padding: widen the whitening conv's output from 24 to 32 channels with 8 zero filters, zero and detached bias, and zero input channels in group-1 conv1. This keeps every output identical while aligning Cin to tensor-core tiles, and cuts mean time on the E036 tip by at least 2%. Accuracy stays within rebuild noise (3-seed mean within 0.1 pp).

E037's cliff comes from freezing before the stem has trained at 32 px (a FixRes-style mismatch), not from total lost group-1 signal. On the E036 tip, starting the group-1 freeze at ~71% of steps, just after the 28→32 px switch at 70% (group-1 LR annealed to 0 by then), loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean vs E036 on the same seeds and cuts time by ~1%. A freeze at 65% (stem never trains at 32 px) would lose at least 0.25 pp.

Staggered FreezeOut cascade: on the E036 tip, also freezing group 2 for the last ~10% of steps (group-2 LR annealed to 0 by then, output detached before group 3, BN kept in train mode, Lookahead averaging every param) cuts mean time by at least 2% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean.

The 24 px bridge is dispensable. On the E036 tip, running 20/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps (E040's schedule) cuts mean time by at least 2% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean vs E036 on the same seeds. E040 read −0.28 pp against E036's selection seeds but only −0.09 pp against fresh seeds, so it is inconclusive (E040~).

Proxy-free loss-based selection: using the main net's own per-sample losses (free from the training forward) to drop the easiest samples from later epochs cuts steps at an accuracy cost no worse than a uniform step trim. Its value depends on whether steps or samples carry accuracy (H5.2). Evidence: E031~ (top-90%: −10.7% time, −0.27 pp held-out, ~2.3 s/pp vs the dial's ~1.5, edge within noise).

On the E036 tip, keeping the 95% highest-loss samples from epoch 2 onward (same mechanism as E031; freeze, detach and resolution points kept as step fractions) cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean vs E036 on the same seeds.

Early in training (the 20/24 px phases), accuracy is carried by the number of optimizer steps under the LR warm-up and peak, not by the pixels processed. Lowering resolution there at a fixed step count is nearly free (E026, E033), while removing steps costs about as much as a uniform trim (E031, E041, both noise-ambiguous). Corollary: the cheap time levers are those that cut per-step cost at a fixed step count.

The opposite prediction to H5.1.3. On the E036 tip, using batch 3000 in the 20/24 px phases (fewer steps, same data passes; SGD lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged) loses at least 0.15 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean vs E036 on the same seeds.

Seesaw-style late batch growth: on the E036 tip, raising the batch from 2000 to 3000 for the last ~15% of steps (in the 32 px frozen phase) while cutting LR there by √1.5 instead of following the linear decay cuts mean time by at least 1.5% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean. It fails if batch 2000 is already above CIFAR-100's critical batch.

Comparisons against a just-kept tip's selection seeds (seeds 3–12) are biased by ~0.1–0.2 pp against the challenger, because the tip was kept on that number (E036: 0.7557 on seeds 3–12 vs 0.7538 on fresh seeds 13–22). So refutations of post-keep changes (E040, E041) are overstated, and baselines must come from seeds not used for selection.

E040 and E041 stacked on the E036 tip (20/28/32 px at 40/0/30/30 with 12 fewer 20 px steps; absolute 28/32 px steps, detach and freeze points unchanged) cut mean time by at least 4.5%. They lose no more than 0.15 pp of the 20-seed mean (seeds 13–32) vs E036 measured on the same 20 seeds.

structured_output.summary:
I revised the tree to match the E036 tip (5.31 s, which passed the local bar on only 1 of its 2 builds) and to apply the review's points on statistics.

**Statistics**
- **Rebuild noise (H4.1):** rewritten. A rebuild moves individual seeds by 0.1–0.44 pp, not the ±0.03 pp the tree said.
- **Winner's curse (H4.1):** E036 scores 0.7557 on seeds 3–12, which were used to keep it, but 0.7538 on fresh seeds 13–22.
- **Tip feasibility (H4):** the unbiased population estimate is ~0.754, so the tip passes the local bar about 55–70% of the time. Keeps should use one fixed gate, measured on seeds not used for selection.
- **Overstated refutations (H4.4, new):** E040 and E041 were compared against E036's inflated seeds 3–12 mean. Against the fresh baseline they lose only about 0.09 and 0.01 pp. H4.2.5 moves from refuted to inconclusive. H2.3.8 (dropping the 24 px phase) and H4.4.1 (E040 and E041 stacked, judged on 20 seeds) are new.
- **H4.3** (local results transfer to the judge) is lowered to 0.4, and **H4.3.2** is set to inconclusive.

**Statuses reconciled with their evidence**
- Supported: H2.6.2 (E034), H2.6.3 (E036), and H2.3.6 (E033 tested its exact statement; E040 tested a different one).
- Refuted: H2.6.4 (E037), H2.6.5 (E039), H1.3.8 (E032).
- H3.2.1 is inconclusive (E035 kept the full whitening set and saved only 0.035 s).
- H3 and H3.2 are retired, since the remaining fixed cost is ~0.02 s on the mean.
- H2, H2.6, H2.3 and H1.3 are rewritten with the current levers and limits. The "early steps carry accuracy" reading of E040/E041 is withdrawn.

**Mechanisms**
- **H6 (uneven per-layer cost):** reworded. E039 places group-1 BN on 15×15 maps and shows it costs nothing, so H6.3 is narrowed to the 31×31 tensors before the pool and lowered to 0.3.
- **H6.1 and H6.2 (small maps, tile alignment):** downgraded. Map-size arithmetic explains E024 and E021 without them.
- **H6.4 (new):** the 24-channel whitening output makes group-1 conv1 inefficient. It has a profiler test (H6.4.1) and a math-identical pad-to-32-channels test (H6.4.2).

**Committee counterexamples**
- E025 and E026 time: both runs were built on E023 while the forecasts assumed E016/E017.
- E028 time: explained by H6.3 or H6.4.
- E030 accuracy: the Lookahead reset is part of the gain (H1.3).
- E032 accuracy: label smoothing 0.3 shapes the averaged solution (H1.3).
- E031 time: selection removes steps, and time follows steps (H2.7 and H5.2, both new).

**Other new branches**
- **Stem freeze:** H2.6.7 (freeze at ~71%, right after the switch to 32 px, to locate E037's cliff) and H2.6.8 (a staggered group-2 freeze).
- **Proxy-free loss selection:** H2.7 and H2.7.1, with E031 as evidence.
- **Batch size and step count:** H5.2 and H5.2.1 (step count carries early accuracy), set up as the opposite prediction to H5.1.3. H5.1.4 (late batch growth) is from the Seesaw paper. H5 is raised to 0.3, and H5.1.x are rebased to E036 with 20-seed judging.

**Other confidence changes**
- H1.3.6 (BN recompute) rises to 0.45: the search confirmed in airbench's code that Lookahead lerps the BN buffers, and the committee is split, so it needs a decisive 20-seed test.
- H1.2.3 and H1.5.4 now point to code reads for the Newton-Schulz step count and filter renormalization.
- Lowered: H1.4, H1.5.5, H1.5.8, H2.3.4, H2.4.

H5 and H6 stay open as Lvl1 hypotheses.
